The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-18 · All platforms · Open-source software

This edition provides 76 complete documentation guides and 51 additional screened leads. 27 earlier screened entries received full guides. New and updated records carry their own dated evidence checks. Creative workflows include optical score recognition, camera-tracked shadow figures, editable voice-and-caption handoffs, subject mattes and depth layers, and editable local image masks. A current AutoShade guide covers material changes in the v1.18 line following the earlier v1.15 review. Software licensing is reviewed independently of model terms, any paid service or required proprietary host. NLLB translation and a browser background-removal route use separate noncommercial model grants. No discovered app was installed or run. The frozen plan covered 110 fields with 1222/1222 repository queries attempted. 1182 completed successfully, 8 were partial, and 32 failed. 227 were bounded. All 29 configured model tasks were attempted. 0 model tasks failed. The collection retained explicit warnings and limits. Metadata screening indexed all 2,543 saved repository pages, spanning 81,587 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog was consulted alongside today's metadata, including earlier pilot candidates. It currently has 113,692 raw records and 1,118 previously screened pending guides. A metadata signal does not establish software eligibility. Unreviewed and excluded candidates remain in private research records. Upstream credential-shaped metadata and signed media queries were redacted before sealing, with original hashes and redaction provenance retained locally. Live primary research beyond GitHub covered all observed fields and the configured ecosystems. The notes identify limits such as access and rate restrictions, failed fetches and bounded discovery pages. The counts represent the documented searches and available pages. The first aggregate pilot repository-tree index was reconstructed from the original saved response bodies; exact initial request timestamps for that aggregate were not recovered. Model-task responses with no rows: text2text-generation. Current cited reviews changed 2 prior labels. Vidyom moved from Quality unverified to Experimental. LiveKit Lite Avatar moved from Quality unverified to Experimental. The separate watchlist and evidence enrichment recorded 59 individual watchlist failures and 3 evidence failures. Source failures are retained as gaps.

Search and review counts

110 creative fields; 1222/1222 repository queries attempted; 29/29 model-task queries attempted. 82328 distinct source candidates and 1275 model leads. 76 detailed profiles and 51 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 32 failed repository queries, 8 partial repository queries, 227 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

Its PyPI release and pre-alpha status support a scoped editor guide. The first guessed license filename returned 404; the actual LICENSE.md was recovered. OpenSlides returned an access error. These are bounded source checks. Source Source Source Source Source

Imaginer’s initial main-branch paths were wrong. The repository specifies master and COPYING. Multiple Codeberg topic search APIs returned 429; current site/file visibility did not clear the incomplete discovery coverage. Source Source Source Source

The local-path dependency is a setup limit for that existing entry. The breadth and installation of other tools were not established from these pages. Source Source Source Source Source

Some guessed package names returned 404. Listings show component/version context without verifying complete source licenses or results. Source Source Source Source Source
  • creative-plugins · searched: Current Interstice and Krita pages give plugin integration context. The SpriteLoom docs separate its original Aseprite route and the MLX or agent adapters. A proprietary creative host, optional model and add-on software keep separate terms and requirements. Source Source Source Source Source

How it uses AI

Vosk turns Mandarin speech into text, then the local Gemma-driven agents select a conversational reply and matching 2D puppet actions for a digital character. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Introduction

Vosk turns Mandarin speech into text, then the local Gemma-driven agents select a conversational reply and matching 2D puppet actions for a digital character. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

What it is good for

Prototype a Chinese-language shadow-theatre character that responds to a typed line or a short spoken scene cue. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Demo & examples

The maintainer links a recorded owner demonstration from the README. It documents intended interaction; response timing and accuracy remain unmeasured here. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Install

Use the documented Python launch with Ollama Gemma 3 4B and a Chinese Vosk model. Resolve the speech-model path in main.py before using voice input. Review the Python imports because the root does not provide an exact environment lock. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Use the documented Python launch with Ollama Gemma 3 4B and a Chinese Vosk model. Resolve the speech-model path in main.py before using voice input. Review the Python imports because the root does not provide an exact environment lock.
ollama pull gemma3:4b
python main.py

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Start the local Ollama service and launch from the working folder. Leave the microphone off and enter a short Chinese line in Text Mode.
  2. Observe the reply and action together. Confirm the compatible Vosk model directory before switching to voice and use Space to start and stop a short recording.
  3. Inspect the recognized text before trusting the response or action. Preserve the animation and cue separately if used as performance reference.

How it uses AI

The Flask server uses rembg and a lightweight U-2-Net ONNX model to isolate foreground images for puppets. Unity renders and animates the figures and phones send collaborative control messages. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Introduction

The Flask server uses rembg and a lightweight U-2-Net ONNX model to isolate foreground images for puppets. Unity renders and animates the figures and phones send collaborative control messages. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

What it is good for

Bring a paper drawing or phone photo onto a projected digital shadow stage, then let collaborators control their figures from phones on a local network. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Demo & examples

The README links an owner video of digital theater. The component guides describe the image processing, renderer and relay. Latency and network stability were not tested. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Install

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Documentation review only; AI Media Scout did not install or run this software. The server lacks a built-in login. The release list did not confirm packaged download links. Owner issues document prior lost articulations and an octave shift, so check notation that changes performance.

How it uses AI

Lilyscan uses Audiveris optical music recognition and Tesseract for score text, repairs common recognition errors and builds editable LilyPond parts for review. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Introduction

Lilyscan uses Audiveris optical music recognition and Tesseract for score text, repairs common recognition errors and builds editable LilyPond parts for review. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

What it is good for

Rescue a printed score or a musician’s photo of a part and compare the scan, proposed engraving and editable source before preparing a rehearsal set. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Demo & examples

The maintainer shows the three-pane review and documents evaluation baselines and import regressions. Those baselines concern the tested corpus. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Install

Follow the Docker guide for its x86-64 Linux server, or build from source with JDK 25 and the Audiveris submodule. Confirm the apt channel or release asset before using a packaged route. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Follow the Docker guide for its x86-64 Linux server, or build from source with JDK 25 and the Audiveris submodule. Confirm the apt channel or release asset before using a packaged route.
docker compose up -d
LANG=C.UTF-8 ./gradlew :lilyscan-cli:shadowJar

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Upload one clean printed page or photo through the local browser interface, ideally for one instrument.
  2. Compare notes and rhythm in the source and engraved panes. Edit the marked LilyPond measures, save and recompile.
  3. Download LilyPond and MusicXML as needed. Cross-check slurs, repeats, octave marks and transpositions against the source.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Hardware
At least 4 GB RAM for x86-64 Linux Docker according to the owner. The documented image is about 700 MB. Total job storage and VRAM requirements are undocumented.
Software
Linux server uses Docker Compose. Native runtime requires Java 25, LilyPond 2.26.0 and full Tesseract language data. Audiveris is bundled in the jar.
Platforms
Docker instructions target x86-64 Linux. Native Linux and Windows are documented. The maintainer marks macOS untested. Browser clients access the configured server.

How it uses AI

A separate LLM agent can read and modify the same text-grid and palette that the human edits in the Tk GUI. The CLI exposes deterministic pixel edits and sprite export to the agent. [1] [2] [3] [4]

Introduction

A separate LLM agent can read and modify the same text-grid and palette that the human edits in the Tk GUI. The CLI exposes deterministic pixel edits and sprite export to the agent. [1] [2] [3] [4]

What it is good for

Draw a constrained palette sprite with a human in the visual editor and an agent making inspectable text edits to the same sprite. [1] [2] [3] [4]

Demo & examples

The README walks through an owner example of a potion-bottle sprite alternating agent edits and GUI refresh. It does not establish quality across other prompts or turnaround times. [1] [2] [3] [4]

Install

Install the PyPI package into a Python environment with Tk support. Initialize a small sprite and open the editor. Use the plain text and CLI route to avoid requiring a specific agent integration. [1] [2] [3] [4]

  1. Install the PyPI package into a Python environment with Tk support. Initialize a small sprite and open the editor. Use the plain text and CLI route to avoid requiring a specific agent integration.
pip install gridfab
gridfab init --size 32x32
gridfab-gui .

First project

Review a small output and the original inputs. [1] [2] [3] [4]

  1. Create a small sprite and define a compact palette.
  2. Ask your selected agent to edit a copy of the grid or perform the documented row and pixel operations.
  3. Refresh the editor, inspect the altered pixels and transparency, and export a PNG or atlas if the result fits.
